1600: from ἐκ and a form of πέτομαι; to fly out, i.e. (by analogy) to extend:--stretch forth.
1601: from ἐκ and πίπτω; to drop away; specially, be driven out of one's course; figuratively, to lose, become inefficient:--be cast, fail, fall (away, off), take none effect.
1602: from ἐκ and πλέω; to depart by ship:--sail (away, thence).
1603: from ἐκ and πληρόω; to accomplish entirely:--fulfill.
1605: from ἐκ and πλήσσω; to strike with astonishment:--amaze, astonish.
1606: from ἐκ and πνέω; to expire:--give up the ghost.
1607: from ἐκ and πορεύομαι; to depart, be discharged, proceed, project:--come (forth, out of), depart, go (forth, out), issue, proceed (out of).
1608: from ἐκ and πορνεύω; to be utterly unchaste:--give self over to fornication.
1609: from ἐκ and πτύω; to spit out, i.e. (figuratively) spurn:--reject.
1610: from ἐκ and ῥιζόω; to uproot:--pluck up by the root, root up.
1611: from ἐξίστημι; a displacement of the mind, i.e. bewilderment, "ecstasy":--+ be amazed, amazement, astonishment, trance.
1612: from ἐκ and στρέφω; to pervert (figuratively):--subvert.
1613: from ἐκ and ταράσσω; to disturb wholly:--exceedingly trouble.
1614: from ἐκ and teino (to stretch); to extend:--cast, put forth, stretch forth (out).
1615: from ἐκ and τελέω; to complete fully:--finish.
1617: neuter of the comparative of ἐκτενής; more intently:--more earnestly.
1620: from ἐκ and τίθημι; to expose; figuratively, to declare:--cast out, expound.
1621: from ἐκ and tinasso (to swing); to shake violently:--shake (off).
1622: from ἐκ; the exterior; figuratively (as a preposition) aside from, besides:--but, except(-ed), other than, out of, outside, unless, without.
1624: from ἐκ and the base of τροπή; to deflect, i.e. turn away (literally or figuratively):--avoid, turn (aside, out of the way).
1625: from ἐκ and τρέφω; to rear up to maturity, i.e. (genitive case) to cherish or train:--bring up, nourish.
1626: from a comparative of ἐκ and (to wound); a miscarriage (abortion), i.e. (by analogy) untimely birth:--born out of due time.
1627: from ἐκ and φέρω; to bear out (literally or figuratively):--bear, bring forth, carry forth (out).
1628: from ἐκ and φεύγω; to flee out:--escape, flee.
1629: from ἐκ and φοβέω; to frighten utterly:--terrify.
1630: from ἐκ and φόβος; frightened out of one's wits:-- sore afraid, exceedingly fear.
1631: from ἐκ and φύω; to sprout up:--put forth.
1632: from ἐκ and (to pour); to pour forth; figuratively, to bestow:--gush (pour) out, run greedily (out), shed (abroad, forth), spill.
1633: from ἐκ and χωρέω; to depart:--depart out.
1634: from ἐκ and ψύχω; to expire:--give (yield) up the ghost.
1636: feminine of a presumed derivative from an obsolete primary; an olive (the tree or the fruit):--olive (berry, tree).
1637: neuter of the same as ἐλαία; olive oil:--oil.
1638: from ἐλαία; an olive-orchard, i.e. (specially) the Mount of Olives:--Olivet.
1639: of Hebrew origin (עֵילָם); an Elamite or Persian:--Elamite.
1640: comparative of the same as ἐλάχιστος; smaller (in size, quantity, age or quality):--less, under, worse, younger.
1641: from ἐλάσσων; to diminish, i.e. fall short:--have lack.
1642: from ἐλάσσων; to lessen (in rank or influence):--decrease, make lower.
1643: a prolonged form of a primary verb (obsolete except in certain tenses as an alternative of this) of uncertain affinity; to push (as wind, oars or dæmonical power):--carry, drive, row.
1645: probably akin to ἐλαύνω and the base of ἐλάσσων; light, i.e. easy:--light.
1646: superlative of (short); used as equivalent to μικρός; least (in size, amount, dignity, etc.):--least, very little (small), smallest.
1647: comparative of ἐλάχιστος; far less:--less than the least.
1648: of Hebrew origin (אֶלְעָזָר); Eleazar, an Israelite:--Eleazar.
1651: of uncertain affinity; to confute, admonish:--convict, convince, tell a fault, rebuke, reprove.
1653: from ἔλεος; to compassionate (by word or deed, specially, by divine grace):--have compassion (pity on), have (obtain, receive, shew) mercy (on).
1654: from ἔλεος; compassionateness, i.e. (as exercised towards the poor) beneficence, or (concretely) a benefaction:--alms(-deeds).
1656: of uncertain affinity; compassion (human or divine, especially active):--(+ tender) mercy.
1657: from ἐλεύθερος; freedom (legitimate or licentious, chiefly moral or ceremonial):--liberty.
1658: probably from the alternate of ἔρχομαι; unrestrained (to go at pleasure), i.e. (as a citizen) not a slave (whether freeborn or manumitted), or (genitive case) exempt (from obligation or liability):--free (man, woman), at liberty.
1659: from ἐλεύθερος; to liberate, i.e. (figuratively) to exempt (from moral, ceremonial or mortal liability):--deliver, make free.
1660: from the alternate of ἔρχομαι; an advent:--coming.
1661: from (an "elephant"); elephantine, i.e. (by implication) composed of ivory:--of ivory.
1662: of Hebrew origin (אֶלְיָקִים); Eliakim, an Israelite:--Eliakim.
1663: of Hebrew origin (אֱלִיעֶזֶר); Eliezer, an Israelite:--Eliezer.
1664: of Hebrew origin (אֵל and הוֹד); God of majesty; Eliud, an Israelite:--Eliud.
1665: of Hebrew origin (אֱלִישֶׁבַע); Elisabet, an Israelitess:--Elisabeth.
1666: of Hebrew origin (אֱלִישָׁע); Elissæus, an Israelite:--Elissæus.
1667: a form of εἱλίσσω; to coil or wrap:--fold up.
1668: probably from ἑλκύω; an ulcer (as if drawn together):--sore.
1669: from ἕλκος; to cause to ulcerate, i.e. (passively) be ulcerous:--full of sores.
1670: probably akin to αἱρέομαι; to drag (literally or figuratively):--draw. Compare ἑλίσσω.
1671: of uncertain affinity; Hellas (or Greece), a country of Europe:--Greece.
1672: from Ἑλλάς; a Hellen (Grecian) or inhabitant of Hellas; by extension a Greek-speaking person, especially a non-Jew:-- Gentile, Greek.
1673: from Ἕλλην; Hellenic, i.e. Grecian (in language):--Greek.
1674: feminine of Ἕλλην; a Grecian (i.e. non-Jewish) woman:--Greek.
1675: from a derivative of Ἕλλην; a Hellenist or Greek-speaking Jew:--Grecian.
1676: adverb from the same as Ἑλληνιστής; Hellenistically, i.e. in the Grecian language:--Greek.
1677: from ἐν and λόγος (in the sense of account); to reckon in, i.e. attribute:--impute, put on account.
1678: of Hebrew origin (perhaps for אַלְמוֹדָד); Elmodam, an Israelite:--Elmodam.
1679: from ἐλπίς; to expect or confide:--(have, thing) hope(-d) (for), trust.
1680: from a primary (to anticipate, usually with pleasure); expectation (abstractly or concretely) or confidence:--faith, hope.
1681: of foreign origin; Elymas, a wizard:--Elymas.
1682: of Chaldean origin (אֱלָהּ with pronominal suffix) my God:--Eloi.
1683: genitive case compound of ἐμοῦ and αὐτός; of myself so likewise the dative case , and accusative case :--me, mine own (self), myself.
1684: from ἐν and the base of βάσις; to walk on, i.e. embark (aboard a vessel), reach (a pool):--come (get) into, enter (into), go (up) into, step in, take ship.
1685: from ἐν and βάλλω; to throw on, i.e. (figuratively) subject to (eternal punishment):--cast into.
1686: from ἐν and βάπτω; to whelm on, i.e. wet (a part of the person, etc.) by contact with a fluid:--dip.
1687: from ἐν and a presumed derivative of the base of βάσις; equivalent to ἐμβαίνω; to intrude on (figuratively):--intrude into.
1688: from ἐν and (to mount; causative of ἐμβαίνω); to place on, i.e. transfer (aboard a vessel):--put in.
1689: from ἐν and βλέπω; to look on, i.e. (relatively) to observe fixedly, or (absolutely) to discern clearly:--behold, gaze up, look upon, (could) see.
1690: from ἐν and (to snort with anger); to have indignation on, i.e. (transitively) to blame, (intransitively) to sigh with chagrin, (specially) to sternly enjoin:--straitly charge, groan, murmur against.
1691: a prolonged form of μέ; me:--I, me, my(-self).
1692: of uncertain affinity; to vomit:--(will) spue.
1693: from ἐν and μαίνομαι; to rave on, i.e. rage at:--be mad against.
1694: of Hebrew origin (עִמָּנוּאֵל); God with us; Emmanuel, a name of Christ:--Emmanuel.
1695: probably of Hebrew origin (compare יֵם); Emmaus, a place in Palestine:--Emmaus.
1696: from ἐν and μένω; to stay in the same place, i.e. (figuratively) persevere:--continue.
1697: of Hebrew origin (חֲמוֹר); Emmor (i.e. Chamor), a Canaanite:--Emmor.
1698: a prolonged form of μοί; to me:--I, me, mine, my.
1699: from the oblique cases of ἐγώ (ἐμοί, ἐμοῦ, ἐμέ); my:--of me, mine (own), my.
